turnaround_reason: Coty was beaten down by a struggling Consumer Beauty division (CoverGirl, Rimmel, Max Factor), excess inventory, tariffs and the loss of the Gucci Beauty license. FY26 is an explicit 'transition year'; the bull case is that its stronger Prestige fragrance portfolio (Burberry, Hugo Boss, Marc Jacobs) drives a return to like-for-like growth in 2H FY26.
bullish_points: Fragrance remains a genuine bright spot in beauty and is the core of Coty's Prestige business
Stock is deeply depressed long term (~35% of its 200-week MA) with revenue still ~$5.8B and 63% gross margins
Management guiding to a return to growth in 2H FY26; Marc Jacobs Beauty relaunch cited as a turnaround driver
Positive free cash flow (~$363M) despite GAAP operating losses
Liquid options (call OI ~5,700) for expressing the view with defined risk
bearish_points: FY26 like-for-like sales still fell ~5%; Q3 guidance calls for another mid-single-digit LFL decline led by Consumer Beauty weakness
Returning the Gucci Beauty license to Kering costs ~$400M ($250M upfront) and removes a revenue stream ~a year early
Net debt is heavy: EV ~$5.9B vs ~$2.4B market cap; leverage limits margin for error
JAB controls ~54%; a controlled company with a large potential overhang and misaligned minority interests
Tariffs and excess inventory continue to pressure gross profit; no insider buying to signal a bottom
catalyst: 2H FY26 inflection back to like-for-like growth, plus Prestige fragrance momentum and Marc Jacobs relaunch traction
catalyst_timing: 2H FY26 (calendar H1 2027); next quarterly print is the near-term read
suggested_trade: Small-to-medium starter spot position; wait for confirmation of the 2H inflection before adding
key_risk: Consumer Beauty keeps deteriorating and the promised 2H growth inflection slips, leaving a levered balance sheet exposed
would_skip_if: Next print shows Prestige/fragrance also decelerating or leverage rising; would pass if the 2H growth guide is walked back
